messages:
alex_support: Hey team, customers started reporting embeddings timeouts on embed-768-v2 around 03:10 UTC. Tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec collapsed (~200 -> ~25). Not seeing obvious 5xx spike, mostly higher latencies and some 429s.
miriam_sre: thx @alex_support. I pulled prod metrics — GPU util is ~92% on the inference pool, avg queue_depth ~46, p90 token latency up but tokens/sec steady. kvcache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 12% around the same time.
deploy-bot: Rollout complete: autosplit-batching v2 -> deploy/infra/2024-11-30T03:05:50Z
dave_infra: curious — autosplit-batching v2 changed kernel selection heuristics (prefer q8_kernel-v3 for shorter sequences). That kernel has higher per-batch overhead; with lots of small batches the effective vectors/sec can tank.
tasha_ml: I can repro a similar effect locally if I force small batch sizes and use q8 kernels. Quick repro (small script):
```bash
# repro (very short inputs)
for i in $(seq 1 500); do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"embed-768-v2","input":"word"}' \
  >/dev/null &
done
wait
```
With q8_kernel-v3 I see average batch size drop to 1.8 and vectors/sec ~30% of expected.
alex_support: logs from prod (snippet):
```
2024-11-30T03:11:12Z enqueue: wait_ms=1203 batch_size=2 kernel=q8_kernel-v3
2024-11-30T03:11:12Z kvcache: miss key=abc123
2024-11-30T03:11:14Z worker: token_generation_ms=15 vector_emit_ms=420 enqueue_timeout=1
```
sam_accounting: customers also reported a flurry of 401s earlier, but our billing service logs show normal activity. I think the 401s were from one client rotating keys rapidly — not correlated with vectors/sec.
miriam_sre: hypothesis: rollout changed kernel selection + autosplit caused more aggressive splitting for short inputs -> tiny batches -> high per-batch overhead + kvcache misses amplify token->vector cost. Need quick mitigations: 1) force previous kernel for embed-768-v2, 2) widen batch_window_ms or reduce autosplit aggressiveness, 3) pin heavy customers to embed-768-v1 temporarily.
lionel_oncall: agree. Action plan: I'll rollback kernel selection on the affected pool to q7-compatible kernel (previous) and increase batch_window_ms to 40ms for the pool. Rolling now to a subset (canary). @deploy-bot can you tag the rollback and throttle the rollout?
deploy-bot: Rollout started: rollback/infra/2024-11-30T03:19:05Z -> target: inference-pool-fsn (canary: 10%)
dave_infra: also recommending a short-term config to raise min_batch_size to 4 for that pool to avoid tiny batches while we debug.
tasha_ml: I'll run the repro after the canary flips and post vectors/sec comparisons. Will also run a KV cache diagnostic to see why hit rate dropped.
alex_support: thanks. I'm messaging affected customers with a brief note and ETA (~30m) and offering to pin them to embed-768-v1 in the meantime.
miriam_sre: follow-up items: create an eval to simulate many short inputs and measure kernel-choice sensitivity; add an alert for sudden kvcache hit-rate drops; add a postmortem if rollback doesn't restore baseline.
lionel_oncall: oncall acked. tagging this for incident review if SLA continues to degrade. keep thread updated.
